# A04 contract requests

Nothing here blocks anything. A04 works today against the contracts as they are.

## 1. Note: additive optional arguments on the writer stubs (no change needed)

The stub signatures are kept, with one optional trailing argument each:

```ts
writeApplication(jobId, campaignId, opts?: WriteOptions)                 // opts: ai, rng, instructions, brief, research, manual
answerQuestion(jobId, question, opts?: { maxChars?, options?, ai?, context? })
```

Callers that pass two arguments get the production behaviour. The extra options
exist for tests, the recorder and the studio's "rewrite with notes".

## 2. Optional: three fields on `ApplicationPacketSchema` (server/contracts/writer.ts)

A07's external API and A05's form engine may want to know which letter went out
without reading `letter_variants`:

```ts
variantId: z.string().optional(),          // letter_variants.id of the chosen letter (also in applications.variant_id)
strategy: LetterStrategy.optional(),       // hook | proof | story
cvPages: z.number().int().optional(),      // measured on the rendered PDF
```

Today these live in `applications.variant_id` and `applications.notes.writer`
(`strategy`, `cvPages`). They are readable through `GET /api/writer/applications/:id`.

## 3. For A10 (not a contract): the v1 applications status filter

The writer saves a job its gates reject as an application with
`status = 'skipped'` and the reason in `applications.reason`, so the owner can
see why it was skipped. The v1 route `GET /api/applications?status=` uses an
enum without `skipped`. Listing all applications works; filtering by `skipped`
needs that value added in `server/routes/applications.ts`.

## Lead decision

1. Noted (additive optional arguments).
2. Approved: variantId, strategy and cvPages added to ApplicationPacketSchema as optional fields.
3. Forwarded to A10.

Also: the autopilot now re-gates at send time through deps.freshPacket (writer loadPacket), so an owner edit that breaks the gates parks the job in needs_you instead of sending the stale packet.
